data_status.label: Development (validation) split · curated examples
data_status.note: Real recordings from the development (validation) split with the saved outputs of one EEG-Jev checkpoint (seed 8, update 13,400). The development split also guided training decisions, so the examples are illustrations, not held-out evidence. Held-out test results are reported in the paper, not on this page.

formal.probabilities_shown: raw model output of the saved prediction files (7 decimals)

seizure_thresholds_dev.rule: lowest raw p(yes) threshold with development window specificity >= 0.99 (primary); Youden J (secondary)

sleep.question: Which sleep stage is assigned to this 30-second EEG epoch under the dataset annotation protocol?
sleep.supervision_meaning: The stage label assigned to this one 30-second epoch by the dataset annotation protocol (W, N1, N2, N3, REM).

input_channels.position_note: Positions are those stored with the encoder features (REVE position bank, metres; x right, y front, z up). A bipolar lead enters the encoder at the position of its first electrode.

seizure.question: Does any annotated seizure interval overlap this 5-second EEG window with positive duration?
seizure.supervision_meaning: Whether any annotated seizure interval overlaps this 5-second window with positive duration; not a seizure fraction and not a majority-of-window rule.

input_channels.position_note: Positions are those stored with the encoder features (REVE position bank, metres; x right, y front, z up). A bipolar lead enters the encoder at the position of its first electrode.
input_channels.empty_slot_note: Input slots of this source that have no lead in the shown recordings; the model input is zero there (checked on 82 model-input windows).

motor_imagery.dataset: Stieger et al. 2021, continuous cursor-control BCI (figshare 13123148)
motor_imagery.question: Which condition was the participant cued to perform in this trial: imagining one of the listed movements, or resting?
motor_imagery.supervision_meaning: The condition the participant was cued to perform in this trial: one of the listed imagined movements or rest. The question does not presuppose that a movement was imagined.

candidate_texts.left_hand: Imagined movement of the left hand
candidate_texts.right_hand: Imagined movement of the right hand

motor_imagery.window_note: The display runs from 2 s before the target appears to 4 s after it. The model reads the 4 s after the target appears (lighter band): 2 s with the target on screen, then the first 2 s of cursor control.
motor_imagery.protocol_note: A cursor-control experiment: imagining the left or the right hand moves the cursor left or right, both hands move it up, and resting moves it down. The label is the cued target, not a measured movement.
motor_imagery.licence_note: The hosting record (figshare) states CC BY 4.0 and the licence file of the authors’ code repository states CC BY-NC 4.0 for code and data; shown here for non-commercial research use, with attribution.

input_channels.position_note: Positions are those stored with the encoder features (REVE position bank, metres; x right, y front, z up). A bipolar lead enters the encoder at the position of its first electrode.

pain.question: What pain intensity did the participant report for this laser-stimulation trial on the 0-to-10 rating scale?
pain.supervision_meaning: The participant's own reported pain rating for this laser-stimulation trial on the 0-10 scale (11 ordered levels); not momentary pain and not laser energy.

scale.name: Numerical rating scale, 0–10
scale.meaning: the participant's own rating of one laser stimulus, given a few seconds after it

input_channels.position_note: Positions are those stored with the encoder features (REVE position bank, metres; x right, y front, z up). A bipolar lead enters the encoder at the position of its first electrode.

pain.ratings_note: The ratings are the per-trial ratings published by the dataset authors in their supplementary repository (github.com/XiangyueZhao/Supplement-Data); the OpenNeuro record itself holds no rating column.

credits_html: EEG excerpts. Sleep staging: Sleep-EDF Database Expanded, version 1.0.0 (Kemp et al., 2000; PhysioNet, doi:10.13026/C2X676). Contains information from the Sleep-EDF Database Expanded, which is made available under the ODC Attribution License v1.0. Seizure detection: CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database, version 1.0.0 (Shoeb, 2009; Guttag, 2010; PhysioNet, doi:10.13026/C2K01R), in the BIDS conversion by Dan and Shoeb (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.10259996; CC BY 4.0). Contains information from the CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database, which is made available under the ODC Attribution License v1.0. Motor imagery: Human EEG Dataset for Brain-Computer Interface and Meditation (Stieger, Engel and He, 2021; figshare, doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.13123148; CC BY 4.0), described in Stieger et al., Scientific Data 8:98 (2021) and Stieger et al., Cerebral Cortex 31:426-438 (2021). Shown for non-commercial research use. Pain rating: OpenNeuro ds005292, version 1.0.0 (Zhao et al., 2024; doi:10.18112/openneuro.ds005292.v1.0.0; CC0); the per-trial pain ratings are those published by the dataset authors in their supplementary repository (github.com/XiangyueZhao/Supplement-Data). PhysioNet: Pollard et al., 2026. The excerpts were filtered, resampled and cut for display by the EEG-Jev authors and are not the original recordings; the dataset authors and hosts do not endorse this demonstration.

publication.note: Waveform files and the per-window data of the case and example files are unchanged from the material build. Descriptive fields were rewritten for publication: model name and checkpoint naming, the name of the split as in the manuscript, input roles instead of build-server paths, schema names; result and timing blocks of earlier drafts were removed because the paper carries the results.
